title: Fill missing values with column mean
instruction:
You have the following dataset with missing values. Fill each NaN with the mean of its column (using np.nanmean), then print the filled array.

Data:
[[ 1.,  2., np.nan],
 [ 4., np.nan,  6.],
 [ 7.,  8.,  9.]]
starter_code:
import numpy as np

data = np.array([[ 1.,  2., np.nan],
                 [ 4., np.nan,  6.],
                 [ 7.,  8.,  9.]])

# Fill NaN with column means
solution_code:
import numpy as np

data = np.array([[ 1.,  2., np.nan],
                 [ 4., np.nan,  6.],
                 [ 7.,  8.,  9.]])

col_mean = np.nanmean(data, axis=0)
for col in range(data.shape[1]):
    mask = np.isnan(data[:, col])
    data[mask, col] = col_mean[col]

print(data)

title: Standardize a dataset
instruction:
Standardize the following dataset (center at mean=0, scale to std=1). Print the standardized array and its new mean and standard deviation (rounded to 2 decimal places).

Data: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
starter_code:
import numpy as np

data = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50], dtype=float)

# Standardize the data
solution_code:
import numpy as np

data = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50], dtype=float)

standardized = (data - data.mean()) / data.std()
print(standardized)
print(f"Mean: {standardized.mean():.2f}, Std: {standardized.std():.2f}")
